question: Population density is calculated as:

options.text: total number of people in a country
average number of people per family
number of persons living per unit area
number of children born per year

solution:
The correct answer is __**number of persons living per unit area**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Population density** is defined as the **number of persons living per unit area**, typically measured in persons per square kilometer or square mile.
 
• It is calculated by dividing the **total population of a region** by its **total land area**.
 
• This metric is used to assess the **concentration of people** in a specific geographic area and helps in understanding the distribution of population.
 
• Population density varies significantly across regions depending on factors like **geography**, **economic activity**, **urbanization**, and availability of **resources**.
 
• For example, countries like **India and China** have high population densities in urban areas compared to rural regions, while countries like **Canada** and **Australia** have lower overall population densities.
